subject: Stratigo throughput regression — executive coordination & customer update
messages:
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2027-09-29T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: [ACTION] Stratigo — sudden throughput drop + rising 5xx rate

Team,

Heads-up: at ~09:50 PT Stratigo reported a sharp throughput regression from ~18k TPS to ~2.2k TPS for their primary inference route (model: redwood-l7-high). Error rate climbed from 0.2% to 6.7% (5xx). I've attached a small telemetry slice (stratigo-telemetry-snippet.csv).

Immediate asks:
- Stand up a short war-room (ops + infra + account) — aiming for 11:00 PT bridge.
- Ben / Neha: quick triage (kernel selection, GPU memory pressure, preemption, autoscale behavior).
- Marissa: draft an immediate customer-facing note acknowledging impact and next steps; we should avoid technical noise but be transparent.
- I'll loop in execs and CS depending on what we see; need an exec readout by 15:30 PT.

Constraints: Stratigo is on a reserved capacity contract (Committed Dedicated) with a 99.9% throughput SLA and a Q4 launch next week — high risk.

I want ownership on the bridge and a one-page exec summary by 15:30. Parking item: if we need to push traffic to a fallback region/model, get cost/impact estimates.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: stratigo-telemetry-snippet.csv (CSV; 48KB; includes request timestamps and 5xx counts)
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-29T10:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Stratigo — sudden throughput drop + rising 5xx rate

On Wed, Sep 29, 2027 at 10:15 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team,
> Heads-up: at ~09:50 PT Stratigo reported a sharp throughput regression ...

Quick triage notes:
- Observed OS-level OOM kills on two nodes hosting the redwood-l7-high shard; memory growth correlates with longer sequence lengths in the last 45m.
- Autoscaler did not provision new nodes due to a recently tightened scaling window (config change from last week).
- Fallback model (redwood-l7-medium-qt8) is compatible and produces ~8-12% longer latencies but stable throughput; we can route traffic there immediately.

Immediate mitigations I can execute:
1) Push an emergency policy to route 30% of Stratigo production traffic to redwood-l7-medium-qt8 (reduces pressure while we fix memory leak).
2) Roll a rolling restart of the two affected nodes (low risk) — will require a brief controlled throughput dip.
3) Relax the autoscale window to allow 2 additional nodes to be provisioned (if capacity available in the pool).

I'll be on the bridge at 11:00 and will execute 1 + 3 unless leadership says otherwise. Estimated stabilization window: 18-45 minutes post-change.

Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachment: mutual-action-plan-v2.pdf (draft MAP for customer communication)

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-29T11:05:00-07:00

Kim / Ben — draft below for customer note. Kept concise and with clear next steps / ETA. Feedback welcome; once approved I can send to Alicia and Gavin at Stratigo.

--- DRAFT CUSTOMER NOTE ---
From: Kimberly Park, Redwood Inference
To: Alicia Ramos, Gavin Lee (Stratigo)
Date: 29 Sep 2027, 11:05 PT
Subject: Update: Degraded throughput — immediate actions and ETA

Hi Alicia / Gavin,

We wanted to acknowledge an ongoing regression affecting your primary inference route. Our engineering team has identified elevated error rates tied to increased memory pressure on a subset of nodes. We have initiated an emergency mitigation plan including routing a portion of traffic to a stable model variant and scaling additional capacity.

What to expect in the next hour:
- Immediate routing of 30% traffic to a validated fallback model to restore baseline throughput (in progress).
- Rolling restarts and autoscaler change to stabilize the cluster; estimated stabilization within 30–60 minutes.
- We will provide a follow-up summary at 17:00 PT with a full incident timeline and next steps.

We recognize the impact to your Q4 launch timeline and are prioritizing this across infra and product leadership. If you prefer, we can open a direct bridge with our CTO and your engineering leads.

Sincerely,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
--- end draft ---

Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager

(Please confirm whether to include exec names in the bridge invite)
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@stratigo.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: gavin.lee@stratigo.com
Date: 2027-09-29T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Update: Degraded throughput — immediate actions and ETA

Kim,

Thanks for the fast response and for the transparency. We are seeing significant production impact on our checkout flow — roughly 14% failed requests correlating with the 5xx spike. Two quick asks from our side: 1) Can you confirm whether this incident will trigger credit under our SLA, and 2) If you route to the fallback model, will output parity be acceptable for our QA gating next week?

We appreciate the offer to put execs on the bridge; Gavin and I are available. Please include a brief note about rollback criteria in your follow-up.

— Alicia
Alicia Ramos
Head of Engineering, Stratigo
From: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
To: alicia.ramos@stratigo.com, gavin.lee@stratigo.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-29T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Stratigo incident — exec readout, customer update, and next steps

Alicia / Gavin / Team,

Exec readout summary (as of 16:45 PT):
- Root cause: memory growth on redwood-l7-high instances under atypical long-sequence workload; two nodes killed by OOM during prefetch.
- Immediate mitigations executed at 11:20 PT: 30% traffic routed to redwood-l7-medium-qt8; autoscale window relaxed and two additional nodes provisioned; rolling restarts performed.
- Results: overall 5xx rate reduced from 6.7% to 0.9% within 40 minutes; throughput returned to ~15.6k TPS (still below peak, under observation).
- Customer impact: transient errors during the 11:15–11:55 window; we estimate 12–15% of requests saw failures during peak.

Planned follow-ups / ownership:
- Ben / SRE: continue observation and heap/profile captures; bug ticket INF-11842 opened and assigned. Estimated patch in 3 days.
- Product: evaluate model variant parity for gating; provide guidance to Stratigo by EOD tomorrow.
- CS (Marissa): schedule a formal SLA review and draft credit estimate; send formal incident report with timeline and MAP by 17:30 PT today.

On credits: we will evaluate SLA impact per contract terms. Marissa, please draft the calculations and proposed credit.

Bridge: Exec bridge scheduled for 17:10 PT (link below) — leadership will attend.

Links / artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-11842, https://drive.redwood.com/open?id=1a2b3c-MAP-v2

Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
